author: Karl Rock
description:
What was life really like more than 5000 years ago at Mohenjo-daro? In this video, I take you inside the Mohenjo-daro Museum in Sindh, Pakistan, to see the incredible artefacts left behind by one of the world's earliest urban civilisations.

Don't miss my full tour of the ancient Mohenjo-daro site:
https://youtu.be/c1mKmeE77Zk

Inside the museum you'll find an extraordinary collection of objects from everyday life, including ancient pottery, copper tools and weapons, stone tools and blades, fishing hooks, ploughs, water vessels, grinding stones, jewellery, beads, seals, toys, musical instruments, children's rattles, combs, mirrors, kohl containers, weights and scales, human and animal remains, and much more.

Irshad is not the person speaking in this video. However, if you’d like a guided tour of Mohenjo-daro, you can contact Irshad directly on WhatsApp: +92 0336 3417 549.

author: Karl Rock
description:
I found this special chole chaat being made right here at Mohenjo Daro, topped with a delicious red imli chutney. And it cost me just Rs. 50 Pakistani rupees, around 18 US cents.

Vegetarian food definitely exists in Pakistan, but it can be harder to find than in India. Pakistan's food culture has a much stronger tradition of eating meat, particularly chicken, mutton and beef, while vegetarian dishes are often based around lentils, vegetables, chickpeas and other pulses.

India is also a country of meat eaters, but vegetarianism has a much stronger cultural and religious presence. Hindu, Jain and Sikh traditions have all contributed to India's long-standing vegetarian food culture. In fact, around 4 in 10 Indian adults describe themselves as vegetarian, while many more avoid particular meats or don't eat meat on certain days.

So finding a plate of chole chaat here in Mohenjo Daro was a pretty good discovery.

And yup, it was delicious.
title: What 18¢ Gets You in Pakistan
